stackOverflowQuestions.title: What is the best architecture for real-time data processing with Apache Flink and edge databases?
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I'm exploring two possible architectures for a real-time data processing pipeline using Apache Flink and edge databases. Approach 1: Flink sinks the processed events into a cloud database. A separate script or service continuously reads new records from the cloud database and processes them in real time. The resulting data is then streamed from Flink to the edge. Approach 2: Flink directly sinks the processed events into a database deployed at the edge. A separate process running at the edge reads the records and processes them on the fly. My questions are: Is the first approach suitable for real-time or near-real-time processing, considering the additional database read/write operations and potential latency? Would the second approach be a more natural and efficient architecture for edge-based real-time processing? What are the recommended best practices for designing such a pipeline in terms of latency, throughput, scalability, and data consistency? I'd appreciate insights into the trade-offs between these two approaches and recommendations for a production-grade architecture.
